events.text: At the top of the white stairs a clerk of the Jade Court sits at a little desk with a long scroll. 'Sect?' None up here. 'House?' None up here. 'Sponsor?' The clerk sighs and writes one character beside your name. Later you learn what it means: 'from below'. Every immortal you pass that day reads it off your face.

choices.text: Thank the clerk and walk on

effects.log: You bow, and the clerk blinks. Few people from below bow to a clerk.

choices.text: Ask what the character means

effects.log: 'Nothing,' the clerk says. 'Only that nobody has vouched for you yet.'

choices.text: Ask for the brush and add your own line

effects.log: You write 'and on the way up' beside it. The clerk lets it stand, appalled.

events.text: Your first night above the clouds you are given a bed in the Newcomers' Pavilion, a long hall on the poorest isle, its roof patched with old cloud. {ln_peer}, in the next bed, came up the stairs a year ago and is still here. 'They look at your boots,' {ln_peer} says. 'The dust of below never quite brushes off. Not to them.'

choices.text: Brush your boots anyway, every morning

effects.log: You brush them for a year. The dust stays; so does the habit, and someone notices.

choices.text: Ask {ln_peer} how to get out of this hall

effects.log: 'Pass something,' {ln_peer} says. 'A trial, a test, a duel. Anything they have to write down.'

choices.text: Sleep, and worry tomorrow

effects.log: You sleep better than anyone in the hall. It is the first thing up here you are best at.

events.text: Your name came up the stairs a little ahead of you, and the Isles have heard it, the way they hear the weather of a distant province. {ln_elder} of {ln_order} comes to the landing to look. 'So you are the one they talked about below,' the old immortal says, and the word 'below' does all the work.

choices.text: Agree that below is where you learned everything

effects.log: 'Then you have a great deal to unlearn,' {ln_elder} says, but stays to talk.

choices.text: Ask what they say about you up here

effects.log: 'Nothing yet,' {ln_elder} says. 'That is what the Isles are deciding.'

choices.text: Say nothing and let the stairs speak

effects.log: You stand at the top of them a while. {ln_elder} goes, thoughtful, without the last word.

events.text: Three sects send someone to the landing to look at you, and none sends anyone to greet you. A disciple of {ln_order} walks around you twice, measuring something with a jade rule, and writes a number down. You ask what the number is. 'Not a large one,' the disciple says kindly, 'for someone from below.'

choices.text: Ask to see the rule

effects.log: It measures roots and foundations. Yours, it says, is good. For below. You hand it back.

choices.text: Thank them for the honesty

effects.log: The disciple reddens. It was not meant as honesty. It reaches {ln_order} that you took it well.

choices.text: Take the rule and measure the disciple

effects.log: The disciple comes out smaller. Their elders are not pleased, but they remember you.

events.text: Your coming was news on every isle: {ln_was}, up the white stairs at last. Half of the Isles turn out to watch, and the other half pointedly do not. At the landing {ln_elder}, a Sovereign of the old school, says in a carrying voice: 'Down there you were a great deal. Up here you are a beginning.' The crowd likes that line very much.

choices.text: Bow and say 'Then I shall begin'

effects.log: The crowd likes that line better. {ln_elder} does not, and that is a start too.

choices.text: Remind them who you were

effects.log: You remind them. They had heard. It does not move the Isles an inch, and you learn something.

choices.text: Walk through the crowd as if it were mist

effects.log: They part for you. Nobody says they did, but they did.

events.text: The Celestial Ministries send a full delegation to meet {ln_was}, with banners, a seat of cloud and a minister who has prepared a speech about the humility proper to those who rise from below. It is a long speech. It is mostly about where to stand. They have prepared a place for you, at the back, with an excellent view of the others.

choices.text: Take the place at the back with grace

effects.log: You stand at the back and see everything. The minister makes a note: not proud. Useful.

choices.text: Ask for the speech in writing

effects.log: You read it twice. Its third paragraph tells you more about the Ministries than any spy could.

choices.text: Thank the minister and go to the front

effects.log: Nobody stops you. Nobody forgets it, either. It costs you a little and teaches them a lot.

events.text: At a tea house on Moonwell Isle the server pours for every table but yours. When you raise a hand, a disciple of {ln_order} at the next table says, not quietly, that the tea here is for those born to the clouds. The server looks at the floor. The floor looks back, sympathetically.

choices.text: Wait until the server comes

effects.log: It takes an hour. When the tea comes it is very good, and the server whispers sorry.

choices.text: Ask the disciple which isle they were born on

ok.log: A poor one, it turns out. The room laughs, and it is not at you.

fail.log: They name a great isle and the room nods. You drink nothing that day.

choices.text: Leave the price of a pot and go

effects.log: You pay for tea you never drank. The server keeps the money, and your face.

events.text: A herald of {ln_order} delivers an invitation to a banquet on Eight Lantern Isle. It is addressed to the person beside you. When the herald sees your face he adds, as an afterthought, that the kitchens are always glad of extra hands. {ln_peer} snorts into a sleeve and then looks guilty about it.

choices.text: Go and help in the kitchens

effects.log: You carry plates all night and hear every secret the guests tell over the soup.

choices.text: Decline with perfect manners

effects.log: Your refusal is so polite that the herald repeats it at the banquet. It is quoted.

choices.text: Go to the banquet anyway, uninvited

effects.log: You sit at the end of a table. Nobody throws you out. Nobody speaks to you either.

events.text: On the cloud road a skiff of {ln_order} comes up behind yours and does not slow down. Its pilot shouts that newcomers from below give way on the road, it is the custom. You have never heard of the custom. You suspect it was invented about a breath ago, for you.

choices.text: Give way and let them pass

effects.log: They pass, laughing. A ferryman who saw it all says you have a long life ahead, and patience suits it.

choices.text: Hold the line of the road

ok.log: The skiff swerves first. Its pilot swears, and remembers your face.

fail.log: The skiff clips yours and you spend a day mending it on a bare rock.

choices.text: Ask the ferryman about the custom later

effects.log: 'There is no custom,' the ferryman says. 'There is only who gives way.' You think about that for years.

events.text: The scripture pavilion on Silverleaf Isle lets anyone read, the sign says. The keeper, {ln_elder}, lets anyone read who can name the immortal who sponsored their ascent. You name nobody, because nobody did. The keeper points you to a shelf of scrolls for beginners. Several of them were written by people from below.

choices.text: Read the beginners shelf from end to end

effects.log: It takes years. Several of the scrolls are wiser than the ones behind the keeper.

choices.text: Ask the keeper who sponsored them

effects.log: {ln_elder} names a great immortal, then admits it was an aunt. Something between you thaws.

choices.text: Copy a scroll from below and give it to the pavilion

effects.log: The keeper reads it twice and files it, grudgingly, on the second shelf.

events.text: You are introduced at a gathering on Pale Heron Isle as 'the one from below', the way one might say 'the one with the cough'. Everyone is very kind about it. One old immortal asks if it is true that people below eat rice every day. Another asks if you miss the dirt. A child asks if you can still die. Everyone hushes the child.

choices.text: Answer the child honestly

effects.log: 'Yes,' you say. 'So can you, only slower.' The child decides you are the best guest there.

choices.text: Talk about rice until they beg you to stop

effects.log: You talk about rice for an hour with great feeling. Some of them go home hungry for it.

choices.text: Ask which of them came from below too

effects.log: Two of them did, a very long time ago. They stop asking you about dirt.

events.text: A matchmaker of the Eight Houses comes to see you, explains at length that no house of the Isles would think of a match with someone from below, and then, lowering her voice, asks whether you have any unmarried kin below who might be strong enough to come up. 'Young blood,' she says. 'From below. It is quite the fashion.'

choices.text: Show her the door, kindly

effects.log: She goes, unoffended. Her trade is never offended. She will come back.

choices.text: Tell her the truth about the world below

effects.log: You talk for an hour. She leaves with a different idea of below, and a cold.

choices.text: Ask what the fashion pays

effects.log: Very well, it turns out. You decline. She is impressed despite herself.

events.text: At a sparring terrace of {ln_order} the young immortals are paired off for practice. You are paired with nobody. The instructor, {ln_elder}, explains that it would be unfair to ask the disciples to strike someone with so fragile a mortal-born foundation. You suspect the unfairness they fear runs the other way.

choices.text: Practise alone at the edge of the terrace

effects.log: You practise alone for a season. By the end, three disciples practise near you, by accident.

choices.text: Offer to spar with the instructor instead

effects.log: {ln_elder} declines with a smile that is not quite a smile, and pairs you the next day.

choices.text: Go and find a terrace that will have you

effects.log: A shabby terrace on a far isle pairs you with anyone. You learn more there.

events.text: A street poet on Lantern Market Isle sings a little song about people from below: their loud voices, their hurry, their habit of dying. The crowd throws stones in the bowl. When the poet sees you listening, the last verse changes, and it is suddenly about people from below who are very good at tipping.

choices.text: Tip the poet, generously

effects.log: The poet adds a verse in your honour. It is mostly about your generosity, and it spreads.

choices.text: Sing the poet a song from below

effects.log: You sing a field song from your youth. The crowd goes quiet, then asks for another.

choices.text: Walk on and let the song be

effects.log: The song follows you for a while, the way songs do, and then forgets you.

events.text: {ln_order} holds its admission test on a stone bridge over nothing. Twelve candidates, one at a time, must carry a full bowl of cloud-water across while an elder asks them questions. The others were born above and have done this since childhood. The examiner, {ln_elder}, sets your bowl a little fuller than theirs.

choices.text: Cross and answer, and spill nothing

ok.log: You cross with the bowl full and every answer right. The examiner writes your name in ink.

fail.log: You spill at the ninth question. The examiner says nothing, which is worse.

choices.text: Point out the fuller bowl, politely

effects.log: The examiner pours a little out without a word. Nobody else saw. You fail anyway, but fairly.

choices.text: Decline this test and wait for another

effects.log: You walk off the bridge. Next year there is another bridge.

events.text: The examiners of the White Stairs give newcomers from below an extra question, by long tradition. Nobody remembers why. This year's extra question, from {ln_elder}, is: 'Why should the Isles take back what the world below sends up?' The other candidates are given a question about tea.

choices.text: Answer the question as asked

ok.log: You answer for an hour. {ln_elder} writes 'pass' and, below it, 'remember this one'.

fail.log: Your answer is honest and long and wrong for the room. They do not write your name.

choices.text: Answer with a story from below

ok.log: The room is silent when you finish. {ln_elder} passes you and asks for the story in writing.

fail.log: They listen politely and pass the candidate after you.

choices.text: Ask for the question about tea

effects.log: 'Of course,' says {ln_elder}. You pass it easily, and learn nothing.

events.text: {ln_order} tests its candidates in its cloud gardens: a hundred spirit herbs grow there, and you must name and tend one for a season without losing it. The herb you are given has died under its last six candidates. They were also from below. The gardener, {ln_peer}, gives you a look that is half warning, half apology.

choices.text: Tend it the way you tended fields below

ok.log: It lives. It flowers, even. The garden writes your name beside the herb.

fail.log: It dies in the frost of the seventh month, as it always does.

choices.text: Ask {ln_peer} why it always dies

effects.log: 'It wants shade from the east,' {ln_peer} whispers. 'Nobody tells the newcomers.'

choices.text: Give the herb back and refuse a rigged test

effects.log: You hand it back, alive. The gardeners talk about that more than any pass.

events.text: The Iron Bell Hall of {ln_order} takes candidates who can ring its bell with their qi alone. Born immortals ring it softly; it is thought vulgar to ring it loudly. You were never taught the soft way. {ln_elder} watches you with the expression of someone who expects a great deal of noise.

choices.text: Ring it softly, the way they do

ok.log: A note like rain. {ln_elder} raises both eyebrows and writes your name.

fail.log: Nothing. The bell does not notice you. The hall does.

choices.text: Ring it as hard as you can

ok.log: It rings for three isles. They pass you, appalled, and complain about it for years.

fail.log: It rings, badly. They do not pass vulgarity.

choices.text: Listen to it first, and come back next year

effects.log: You sit by the bell all day. Next year you will know how.

events.text: An admission test of {ln_order} is a game of weiqi against {ln_elder}, who has not lost in three thousand years and plays with the cheerful cruelty of someone who will not lose today. A newcomer from below is not expected to win. A newcomer from below is expected to resign with grace by the fortieth move.

choices.text: Play the long game

ok.log: You lose by half a point at the three hundredth move. {ln_elder} passes you and asks for a rematch.

fail.log: You resign at the eightieth move, later than expected. Not later enough.

choices.text: Resign with grace at the fortieth move

effects.log: You resign on cue. They pass nobody who resigns on cue, but they think well of you.

choices.text: Ask {ln_elder} to teach you instead

effects.log: The old immortal is so surprised that you are given a lesson. You learn a great deal and pass nothing.

events.text: The Cloud Legion's recruiting test is simple: stand on the outer rail of a war barge for a night of storm. Born immortals tie themselves on with silk. A sergeant of {ln_order} takes your silk away, with a grin, 'so we can see what below is made of'. {ln_peer}, beside you, quietly ties a second knot in theirs.

choices.text: Stand the night with nothing

ok.log: Dawn finds you on the rail. The sergeant gives the silk back, and a nod worth more.

fail.log: A gust takes you off at the fourth bell. You land on a lesser isle, bruised.

choices.text: Share {ln_peer}'s silk

effects.log: You tie on with {ln_peer} and you both stand the night. They fail you both and like you both.

choices.text: Climb down before the storm

effects.log: You climb down. 'Sensible,' the sergeant says, as an insult. You are dry.

events.text: {ln_elder}, a Golden Immortal of {ln_order}, has a habit: each newcomer from below is offered one bout on the Terrace of Correction, to learn how the Isles do things. It is not a cruel habit, the elder says. It is only thorough. Forty newcomers have learned. Three of them could walk afterwards.

choices.text: Accept the bout

ok.log: You walk off the terrace and the old one does not. The Isles learn something.

fail.log: You are corrected, thoroughly. You can walk, which puts you among the three.

choices.text: Thank the elder and decline

effects.log: 'Wise,' says {ln_elder}. 'For below.' The word follows you for years.

choices.text: Ask to watch a bout first

effects.log: You watch {ln_elder} correct someone else. You learn how the old one breathes before a strike.

events.text: Someone has written your name on the challenge board of Thunder Step Isle: 'the one from below will find that dust does not fly'. It is signed {ln_elder}, an immortal of {ln_order} who has never lost to anyone born beneath the clouds, and says so on the board as well, in smaller writing.

choices.text: Answer the board

ok.log: Dust flies, it turns out. You write your name over the old one's.

fail.log: You lose, and the board is updated in small writing.

choices.text: Write beneath it: "Not yet"

effects.log: You write it and walk away. The board keeps your two words for a century.

choices.text: Leave the board be

effects.log: The writing stays. People read it. You let them.

events.text: At a wedding feast {ln_elder}, a Heavenly Immortal and very drunk, announces that people from below are lucky to be let up the stairs at all, and offers to show the whole hall why. The hall is delighted. The bride is not. The old one's sleeve is already rolled back, and looking at you.

choices.text: Take it outside, into the garden

ok.log: You win in the garden and walk back in before the soup is cold.

fail.log: You lose in the garden, quickly, and come back for the soup.

choices.text: Toast the bride instead, loudly

effects.log: You toast the bride so well the hall forgets the old one. The bride does not forget you.

choices.text: Leave the feast

effects.log: You leave. The old one takes it as a win and tells everyone, for years.

events.text: {ln_elder} of {ln_order} does not challenge you. The old immortal simply walks into the pavilion you rent, sits in your chair, drinks your tea and reads your letters, and waits to see what you will do. It is how the old ones put a newcomer in their place, {ln_peer} warns: they take the place first.

choices.text: Take the chair back by force

ok.log: The chair is yours again. The old one bows, for the first time in centuries.

fail.log: You end up on the floor. The old one finishes the tea.

choices.text: Pour more tea and wait them out

effects.log: You pour tea for nine days. On the tenth the old one leaves, and sends you a better pot.

choices.text: Move to another pavilion

effects.log: You give up the pavilion. You keep the letters. It is a fair trade, nearly.

events.text: A senior disciple of {ln_order}, born above and very proud of it, challenges you to race the cloud road from Jade Gate to the Far Isle. The prize, the disciple says, is that the loser stops claiming to belong up here. Half the isle has come to watch. {ln_elder}, the disciple's master, has come to watch the disciple win.

choices.text: Race, and do not hold back

ok.log: You reach the Far Isle with time to buy tea. The master pays for it.

fail.log: You come second, close enough that nobody laughs. Nearly nobody.

choices.text: Race, and let it be close

ok.log: You win by a hair, and the disciple keeps face. The master notices both.

fail.log: You lose by a hair, as planned, and the plan does not feel clever.

choices.text: Refuse a race for such a prize

effects.log: You refuse. The prize was always a fool's; some of the crowd see it.

events.text: {ln_elder} has been sent by {ln_order} to put you in your place, which is a phrase you have heard before but never seen done so courteously. The old immortal brings a gift, a chair of cloud-wood, very low. 'For you to sit in, when you are received,' the elder says. 'Unless you would rather show me you need a taller one.'

choices.text: Show the elder

ok.log: The elder takes the low chair home. A taller one comes the next morning.

fail.log: You sit in the low chair for a long while afterwards, thinking.

choices.text: Sit in the low chair and say thank you

effects.log: You sit in it at every reception for a century. It becomes a famous chair.

choices.text: Give the chair to {ln_peer}

effects.log: {ln_peer} sits in it with dignity. The elder is put out; the chair was meant for you.

events.text: An old immortal of {ln_order} stops you on a bridge and asks you to step aside. You do. The old one asks you to step aside again. You do. On the third time {ln_elder} smiles and says: 'Below, you would have struck me by now. Good. I wanted to see how far down the dust goes.'

choices.text: Ask how far down it goes

effects.log: 'Further than you think,' {ln_elder} says, 'and further than they think.' You walk on together.

choices.text: Step aside no further

ok.log: You hold the bridge. The old one laughs and lets you have it.

fail.log: You learn how little the bridge needed you.

choices.text: Step aside a fourth time

effects.log: You step aside. The old one is disappointed, and you are a little too.

events.text: The Isles keep a very old custom: a newcomer who has lived above for a while may challenge one immortal of a rank above for the right to be called by name instead of 'the one from below'. Most never dare. {ln_elder} of {ln_order}, a rung above you, has been waiting for someone to dare for a thousand years.

choices.text: Dare

ok.log: You win your name. The Isles call you by it from that day.

fail.log: You lose, and keep the old name a while longer. It is lighter than you feared.

choices.text: Ask {ln_elder} who dared last

effects.log: 'I did,' says {ln_elder}. 'I lost. They call me by my name anyway now.'

choices.text: Wait for a better year

effects.log: You wait. The custom is patient. It has outlasted everyone who invented it.

events.text: A scholar of the Isles is writing a book on the world below, and comes to interview {ln_was}. The scholar has never been below and has opinions about it. Every story you tell is written down slightly wrong and corrected into something more like what the scholar expected. The book will sell very well.

choices.text: Correct every story, patiently

effects.log: The book comes out truer than it would have. It sells less well, and lasts longer.

choices.text: Let the scholar have the stories they want

effects.log: The book is a success. In it you are taller, crueller and dead.

choices.text: Write your own account

effects.log: You write it. Nobody above reads it for a century; then everybody does.

events.text: Below, you were {ln_was}, and people stood when you came in. Up here, at the Jade Court's spring audience, you stand for an hour in the outer court among clerks and newcomers while the factions go in. {ln_elder}, a minister passing, recognises you from the stories. 'Ah,' the minister says. 'It is different here, is it not?'

choices.text: Say 'It is, and it was right to be'

effects.log: The minister stops, surprised, and talks with you until the audience is over.

choices.text: Say nothing and wait your hour

effects.log: You wait the hour. Some of the clerks remember who waited without complaint.

choices.text: Say it was better below

effects.log: You say it. It is a little true. The minister passes on, smiling.

events.text: A seat you held below meant something there. Up here an old immortal of {ln_order} asks you to describe it, and listens, and then explains that a seat below is like a seat at a children's table: honourable, and nobody minds who sits in it. 'But you will have learned to govern,' {ln_elder} adds. 'That is not nothing. Show us.'

choices.text: Offer to run something small, as a start

effects.log: They give you a ferry to run. It is the best-run ferry on the Isles within the year.

choices.text: Tell them how the seat was really held

effects.log: You tell them about the hard years. {ln_elder} listens to the end.

choices.text: Say the children ran it well

effects.log: 'Did they,' says {ln_elder}, and for once has nothing to add.

events.text: Your name came up the stairs before you, and it was not a kind one. A mother on Willow Isle pulls her child inside when you pass. A stallholder will not sell to you. {ln_elder}, an old immortal, tells you plainly: 'Up here nobody minds what you did below. We mind that you might do it here.'

choices.text: Do nothing here they could mind

effects.log: You live quietly for a decade. The mother lets the child stay out.

choices.text: Tell {ln_elder} what really happened

effects.log: The old immortal hears it out and says it is worse than the story, and better.

choices.text: Let them be afraid

effects.log: Fear is a kind of respect, you decide. It is a lonely kind.

events.text: Nobody up here has heard of you, and you find that you mind. {ln_peer}, who came up a year after you, is already known on three isles because a sect below writes letters about them. Nobody below writes about you. Nobody above asks. The clouds do not care what you were. That might be a gift.

choices.text: Take the gift: begin clean

effects.log: You begin clean. It is lighter than you expected.

choices.text: Write a letter below yourself

effects.log: Someone below writes back. It is a short letter, and you keep it.

choices.text: Make a name here, from nothing

effects.log: You set out to. The Isles have seen it done before; they watch to see if you can.

events.text: A troupe on Lantern Market Isle performs a play about {ln_was}. It is very popular. In it you are played by a handsome immortal who wins every fight and weeps at every funeral. At the end, the character climbs the white stairs and is welcomed by everyone. The audience, who did not welcome you, applaud this part loudest.

choices.text: Go backstage and thank the actor

effects.log: The actor is mortified, then delighted. The next run ends a little differently.

choices.text: Point out that nobody welcomed you

effects.log: You say it aloud in the hall. The applause stops. Some of them look ashamed.

choices.text: Buy a ticket for tomorrow

effects.log: You watch it three times. By the third, you have stopped minding.

events.text: {ln_order} has written your name in the lighter ink. The first labour of a newcomer: sweep the Hall of Ancestors every dawn for a year, under the eyes of the portraits, who were all born above. {ln_elder} inspects the floor each morning with a white silk cloth.

choices.text: Sweep it until the cloth stays white

effects.log: A year of dawns. On the last day {ln_elder} folds the cloth away unused.

choices.text: Sweep, and talk to the portraits

effects.log: You tell them about below. On the last day one of them seems to be smiling.

choices.text: Refuse a labour meant to shame

effects.log: {ln_elder} writes something next to your lighter ink. The probation waits.

events.text: The second labour: escort a supply skiff of {ln_order} to its outpost on the Mistreach, through cloud reavers' water, with a crew that was told you will get them all killed. The quartermaster, {ln_peer}, gives you the worst skiff in the yard and says it is a mark of respect.

choices.text: Take it through the Mistreach

ok.log: The skiff arrives. The crew stops talking about getting killed.

fail.log: The reavers take half the cargo. You bring the crew home whole, which counts.

choices.text: Fix the skiff first, with your own hands

effects.log: Three days of work and a borrowed tool. The crew watches; the trip goes easily.

choices.text: Ask for a better skiff

effects.log: You do not get one. You do get a reputation for asking.

events.text: The third labour of {ln_order}: sit at the Vigil of the Silent Cloud for a hundred days with the order's own disciples, who were born above and have been taught to sit still since they could walk. You were taught to plough. {ln_elder} expects you to fidget by the tenth day, and has told someone so.

choices.text: Sit the hundred days

ok.log: A hundred days. On the last one a disciple fidgets, and it is not you.

fail.log: You fidget on the ninetieth day. They count it as done, sourly.

choices.text: Sit, and plough a field in your head

effects.log: You plough a thousand fields in your head. The hundred days pass like a season.

choices.text: Ask who {ln_elder} told

effects.log: {ln_elder} tells you. You do not fidget out of spite. It is not the point of the vigil.

events.text: One labour {ln_order} sets newcomers is to carry the order's letter to a rival faction and come back with an answer, without starting a war. Born members go with an escort. You go alone, because it is a labour. {ln_elder} of the rival faction reads the letter, then looks at you, then reads it again.

choices.text: Win the answer with good words

ok.log: You come back with an answer, and an invitation to tea. They are both impressed.

fail.log: You come back with an answer, and a long complaint about the messenger.

choices.text: Wait in the rival hall until they answer

effects.log: Nine days. On the tenth, an answer. On the eleventh, you are home.

choices.text: Leave the letter and go

effects.log: They answer nothing, and {ln_order} counts that as nothing.

events.text: A newcomer's labour for {ln_order}: tend the order's oldest elder, {ln_elder}, through a long seclusion. The old immortal hates people from below, is sure you will poison the tea, and sends every cup back. The labour, the steward explains, is not the tea. The labour is lasting the seclusion.

choices.text: Bring tea every morning regardless

effects.log: Two hundred cups sent back. The two hundred and first is kept. Then all of them are.

choices.text: Taste each cup first, in front of the door

effects.log: You taste every cup. On the fortieth day the door opens, and the old one drinks.

choices.text: Leave the tea outside and stop knocking

effects.log: The old one notices the silence and is offended by it. It does not count.

events.text: The last thing {ln_order} asks of a newcomer is a gift from below, something the Isles do not have. Born members bring nothing; the custom is only for those who climbed. {ln_peer}, who came up the stairs before you, brought a sack of seed rice. It grows on the outer isle still. Everyone there is quietly proud of it.

choices.text: Give them a song from below

effects.log: You teach it to the youngest disciples. It is sung at festivals, wrongly, forever.

choices.text: Give them a technique from below

effects.log: You show a form the Isles never had. Three elders argue about it for a century.

choices.text: Give them seed of your own

effects.log: A small orchard on a poor isle. The order picks its fruit with you every autumn.

events.text: The academy's examination hall is full of candidates born above, who brought their own brushes, their own ink, their own servants to grind it. You brought a brush you made yourself, below, out of a fox's tail and patience. The proctor, {ln_elder}, looks at it the whole first hour. At the end of the day the proctor asks to hold it.

choices.text: Let the proctor hold it

effects.log: The old proctor turns it over, says nothing, and hands it back very carefully.

choices.text: Offer to make the proctor one

effects.log: You make one in a month. The proctor uses it for the rest of a very long life.

choices.text: Put it away before anyone else asks

effects.log: You keep it close. Some things from below are not for the Isles.

events.text: After the examination, the academy posts its list. Newcomers from below are listed on a separate board, beside the gate, where the rain comes in. {ln_peer} finds a name on it and cries. You read the board twice and find a dozen people you would want to know, all of them standing in the rain.

choices.text: Stand in the rain with them

effects.log: You all stand there until the rain stops. It is the first friendship you make above.

choices.text: Ask the academy to move the board

effects.log: They say it was always there. Next year it is under the eaves.

choices.text: Go home and study for next year

effects.log: You study through the winter. Your brush improves; so does your mood.

events.text: The academy's oldest examiner, {ln_elder}, reads your paper aloud to the others, which is not done. The others listen with the faces of people who have decided not to be impressed. When {ln_elder} reaches the end, nobody speaks. 'From below,' someone says finally, as if that explains it. 'Yes,' says {ln_elder}. 'Isn't it.'

choices.text: Bow to the examiners

effects.log: You bow. The oldest one bows back, which has not happened in an age.

choices.text: Ask which part they disliked

effects.log: They tell you. They are wrong about two parts and right about one, and you keep that one.

choices.text: Leave before anyone can say more

effects.log: You go. The examiners argue all night, which is what {ln_elder} wanted.

events.text: {npc} came up the white stairs to be with you, and the Isles look at {him} the way they looked at you, only worse: the spouse of a newcomer from below is a newcomer twice over. At a gathering of {ln_order} a hostess seats {npc} among the servants' children, and is very sorry, and does not move {him}.

choices.text: Go and sit with {npc}

effects.log: You sit among the children too. They are good company. The hostess is mortified.

choices.text: Let {npc} handle it

effects.log: {npc} tells the children a story so good the hostess comes to listen. {He} needed no help.

choices.text: Say nothing and stay where you are seated

effects.log: {npc} says nothing either, all the way home. It is a long road.

events.text: Someone on the Isles has asked {npc}, in your hearing, whether {he} married you before or after you were anybody, and what {he} was before that. {npc} answers that {he} was a person. The asker, {ln_elder}, laughs and says that below, perhaps, that is enough.

choices.text: Tell {ln_elder} that up here it should be too

effects.log: You say it clearly, and the room hears. It costs you; it was worth it.

choices.text: Take {npc} home and make tea

effects.log: {npc} drinks it and laughs about it later. Much later.

choices.text: Answer for {npc} with wit

ok.log: The room laughs with you, and at {ln_elder}. {npc} squeezes your hand.

fail.log: The room laughs, but not with you. {npc} looks tired.

events.text: {npc} is of your blood and came up after you, and the young immortals of the Isles have found a word for {him}: second-dust, because {he} is the dust of the dust. {He} has stopped going to the terraces. {He} pretends not to care, the way you used to pretend.

choices.text: Go to the terraces with {npc}

effects.log: You practise beside {npc} every morning. The word fades, because nobody dares.

choices.text: Teach {npc} the word means nothing

effects.log: You talk all night. {He} goes back alone, and that is better.

choices.text: Find {npc} a terrace with other newcomers

effects.log: {He} finds friends there. The second-dust practise together, and grow fast.

events.text: A school on the Isles refuses {npc}, who is your kin and came up the stairs, on the grounds that the blood of newcomers is 'unsettled'. {ln_elder}, its headmaster, says this with real regret, and offers {npc} a place sweeping the school instead, so that {he} may at least breathe the air.

choices.text: Vouch for {npc} at the school gate

effects.log: You stand at the gate for a day. {npc} is let in, on trial. You are not thanked.

choices.text: Let {npc} take the broom, and learn

effects.log: {npc} sweeps and listens. In three years {he} knows more than the students.

choices.text: Teach {npc} yourself

effects.log: You teach {him} every evening. It is not a school. It is better.

events.text: {npc}, your student from below, climbed the white stairs after you and is now nobody twice: a newcomer, and the student of a newcomer. A senior of {ln_order} asks {npc} to fetch water, then to fetch it again, then laughs. {npc} fetches it a third time without a word, and looks at you as {he} passes.

choices.text: Take the bucket and fetch it yourself

effects.log: You fetch it. The senior goes very quiet. {npc} does not look away again.

choices.text: Let {npc} fetch it; it's {his} road

effects.log: {npc} fetches it a fourth time, smiling. The senior stops asking.

choices.text: Speak to the senior later, alone

effects.log: You speak politely, alone. The senior apologises to {npc}, briefly.

events.text: {npc} has asked you, quietly, whether {he} should stop telling people whose student {he} is. It would be easier, {he} says, to be an orphan of the Isles than the student of the one from below. {He} is not wrong. You see it in the way doors open a little slower for {him}.

choices.text: Tell {him} to say your name loudly

effects.log: {He} says it at every door. Slowly, the doors learn it.

choices.text: Tell {him} to do as {he} thinks best

effects.log: {He} chooses to say it anyway. It is the best thing {he} has done.

choices.text: Tell {him} to stop

effects.log: {He} stops. Doors open faster, and something between you closes a little.

events.text: {npc} came up the white stairs, met you, and was given the same character beside {his} name that you were given. The Isles look at {him} as they looked at you at first: dust on the boots, below in the voice. {npc} laughs about it, and asks you how long it lasts.

choices.text: Introduce {npc} at your side, everywhere

effects.log: Where you go, {npc} goes. Being looked down on is lighter shared.

choices.text: Tell {npc} the truth: as long as it takes

effects.log: 'Then I will take it,' {npc} says, and does.

choices.text: Warn {npc} which isles to avoid

effects.log: {He} avoids them for a century, then goes anyway and does well.

events.text: {npc} has only just come up the white stairs, and is having the welcome you had: none. {ln_elder} of {ln_order} asks {npc}, at the landing, who sponsored the climb. {npc} looks around for an answer and finds you standing there, a few years less of a newcomer than {he} is.

choices.text: Say: 'I do'

effects.log: The old immortal writes your name beside {his}. It is worth less than it should be. It is worth something.

choices.text: Let {npc} answer

effects.log: 'Nobody,' says {npc}, with a grin you remember. {ln_elder} writes the character.

choices.text: Walk {npc} past the desk

effects.log: You walk {him} past it, and the clerk does not stop either of you. Nobody expected that.

events.text: One morning a herald of {ln_order} comes to your door with an invitation, and the name on it is yours, spelled right, with no character beside it. You read it twice. You cannot remember the last time anyone on the Isles said 'from below' in your hearing. You did not notice when it stopped. Nobody does.

choices.text: Go, and sit where they seat you

effects.log: They seat you in the middle of the table. You are not new here any more.

choices.text: Go, and bring a newcomer with you

effects.log: {ln_peer} sits beside you, dust on the boots. You are the one who vouches now.

choices.text: Keep the invitation and stay home

effects.log: You keep it in a box with the clerk's first scroll. Both are history now.

events.text: At the top of the white stairs there is a new face, out of breath, dust to the knees, looking around at the Isles as you once did. The clerk at the little desk asks: 'Sect? House? Sponsor?' The newcomer has none. The clerk raises the brush. Then the clerk sees you watching, and waits to see what you will say.

choices.text: Say: 'I will sponsor them'

effects.log: The clerk writes your name, and no character. The newcomer will remember it all their life.

choices.text: Say nothing, and let the newcomer begin

effects.log: The brush writes the character. The newcomer begins, as you did. It is a beginning.

choices.text: Ask the clerk to retire the character

effects.log: 'It is older than both of us,' the clerk says. 'But I will write it smaller.'

events.text: {ln_elder}, who corrected you once on a terrace, or tried to, comes to you with a question about the world below, and asks it as one asks a colleague. The Isles, it seems, have decided about you. It took years. It will take the next newcomer as long. You find you are glad it took you that long.

choices.text: Answer as a colleague

effects.log: You talk until dark, as equals. It is the first time, and not the last.

choices.text: Remind {ln_elder} of the terrace

effects.log: {ln_elder} laughs until the cups shake. Old enemies are the best friends above the clouds.

choices.text: Answer, and ask a favour for a newcomer

effects.log: The favour is granted. The newcomer never learns who asked.

events.text: At the Isle Bazaar the stallholder names a price, looks at your sleeve for a faction's badge, finds none, and names a higher one. The immortal beside you, wearing the crane of {ln_order}, pays the first price for the same thing and does not notice the difference. The stallholder does not hide it. That is the custom: no backing, no discount.

choices.text: Pay the higher price

effects.log: You pay. The stallholder thanks you, almost warmly.

choices.text: Ask the immortal to buy it for you

effects.log: The immortal laughs and does it. You owe a favour to a stranger now.

choices.text: Walk away

effects.log: You walk away. The stall is not the only one; every stall is the same.

events.text: The great hall of {ln_order} is holding a lecture by a Sovereign, open to every immortal of a faction, a house or a sect. The door warden asks yours. You have none. The warden is kind, and shows you a window in the garden wall where people with none can listen, if they are quiet.

choices.text: Listen at the window

effects.log: You hear every word, better than those inside, who are talking.

choices.text: Ask the warden what the Sovereign was, once

effects.log: 'A rogue,' the warden admits. 'Twenty thousand years ago.' You listen at the window, smiling.

choices.text: Go home

effects.log: You go home. The lecture is printed later. You read it in a draughty room.

events.text: A ferryman of the cloud roads charges by the head: one price for the badged, another for the unbadged. He explains it is not his rule. 'Who stands behind you, if I sink?' he asks. 'Nobody comes looking for a rogue.' He says it plainly, the way a ferryman says the weather.

choices.text: Pay the unbadged price

effects.log: You pay it. The ferry does not sink.

choices.text: Fly the road yourself

effects.log: You fly the long way. It takes a day and you see three isles you never knew.

choices.text: Ask him who comes looking for him

effects.log: 'Nobody,' says the ferryman. He takes you for the badged price.

events.text: An immortal of {ln_order} has accused you of stealing a cloud-herb from the order's terraces. You did not. But a rogue has nobody to speak for them at the Jade Court's lower bench, and the clerk asks, without malice, whether you would like to simply pay for the herb and save everyone the trouble.

choices.text: Pay, and be done with it

effects.log: You pay for a herb you never took. The clerk is relieved. You are not.

choices.text: Speak for yourself at the bench

ok.log: You speak for an hour. The accuser drops the matter, red-faced.

fail.log: The bench finds for the order. Rogues usually lose; you lose.

choices.text: Find the real thief

effects.log: It was a crane. You bring the feather. The order apologises, a little.

events.text: A rich house of the Isles hires rogues for its dangerous errands, because nobody avenges a rogue. The steward says this frankly, as an advantage of the job. The pay is good. The errand is to fetch something from an old immortal's cave that three of the house's own declined to enter.

choices.text: Take the errand

ok.log: You bring it back. The house pays well and remembers you, as useful.

fail.log: The cave keeps its secret and a little of your health.

choices.text: Decline: no house bets on you

effects.log: You decline. The steward is surprised; rogues usually need the money.

choices.text: Ask for the house's badge as payment

effects.log: The steward laughs. A rogue asking to stop being a rogue is funny, apparently.

events.text: You are turned away from the Moon Pavilion on Silver Tide Isle: it receives only immortals of a faction, a sect or a house. {ln_peer}, who was a rogue until last spring, is let through ahead of you, wearing a new badge and an apologetic face. Last spring you shared a draughty room.

choices.text: Wave {ln_peer} on, without bitterness

effects.log: {ln_peer} goes in, and comes out early with two cakes, one for you.

choices.text: Ask {ln_peer} what the badge cost

effects.log: 'Everything I said I would never give,' says {ln_peer}. 'And a little more.'

choices.text: Wait outside the door, in plain view

effects.log: You wait all evening. The pavilion finds it embarrassing, which is the idea.

events.text: A matchmaker will not take your name. A tailor makes you wait behind three apprentices of {ln_order}. A tea house seats you by the door. None of it is cruel. All of it is the custom of the Isles: an immortal alone is an immortal of no account. You notice it most on the days you do not mind it.

choices.text: Let the custom be the custom

effects.log: You stop counting the slights. You have more years than they have customs.

choices.text: Keep a list, for later

effects.log: You keep a list, neatly. It is a long list, and one day it may be useful.

choices.text: Seek out other rogues

effects.log: There are more of you than the Isles admit. You drink together on a poor isle, often.

events.text: On a poor isle at the edge of the clouds a dozen rogues share a fire: immortals of no faction, no sect, no house. One was a great sect master below. One was a servant. Up here they are the same: charged more, seated last, free. {ln_peer} passes you a cup and asks if you mean to stay one of them.

choices.text: Say: 'For as long as I like'

effects.log: The fire cheers. You are of no account together, which is a kind of account.

choices.text: Say: 'Until I find a house worth it'

effects.log: They nod. Most of them say that. Some of them mean it.

choices.text: Sit, and listen to their stories

effects.log: You hear a dozen roads up the white stairs. Each is worth a book.

events.text: The Isles' spring tide of cloud-fish comes in, and every faction sends its nets. Rogues fish from the rocks, where the fish are thin, because the good water is held by those with backing. A warden of {ln_order} comes to move you on even from the rocks. 'For your safety,' the warden says.

choices.text: Move on, politely

effects.log: You move on and fish in a worse place. The fish there are worse too.

choices.text: Stay on the rock and keep fishing

ok.log: The warden gives up. You fish all day and eat well.

fail.log: The warden pushes. You fall in, cold and annoyed.

choices.text: Offer the warden your best fish

effects.log: The warden takes it and leaves you be. Bribery: the backing of rogues.

events.text: A child of the Isles asks you, very seriously, why you have no badge. Everyone has a badge, the child says. Even the cook has a badge. The child's mother pulls the child away and apologises in the voice people use for apologising to beggars.

choices.text: Tell the child the truth

effects.log: 'I have not found one I like,' you say. The child decides this is the most daring thing ever said.

choices.text: Make the child a paper badge

effects.log: The child wears it for a year. It says, in a child's hand, YOUR OWN.

choices.text: Say nothing, and let them go

effects.log: You let them go. You think about badges all evening.

events.text: The Jade Court's census of the Isles arrives. Under 'faction', 'sect' and 'house' you write nothing. The census clerk explains that the form has no line for nothing, and writes you down under 'miscellaneous', between a talking crane and a cloud that is thought to be a person.

choices.text: Accept miscellaneous

effects.log: You are miscellaneous for a century. It is quite good company.

choices.text: Ask for a new line on the form

effects.log: The clerk sends it up. In three hundred years the form has a line: Unbound.

choices.text: Meet the talking crane

effects.log: The crane is a rogue too. It knows every road of the Isles, and tells you some.

events.text: A faction of the Isles is recruiting, and its recruiter makes you an offer: a badge today, no trial, a rank of the lowest. The price is a vow you do not like. {ln_peer}, who took such a badge, tells you it is lighter than it looks for the first hundred years and heavier after.

choices.text: Refuse the vow

effects.log: You stay a rogue, charged more and seated last. You sleep well.

choices.text: Ask for time to think

effects.log: The recruiter gives you a year. Recruiters are very patient with rogues.

choices.text: Ask {ln_peer} about after

effects.log: {ln_peer} talks till dawn. You learn what a badge weighs.

events.text: A paper crane finds you on a bare rock of the Isles where you are drifting, as drifters do. Inside is a child's writing: Reedwater Isle has no faction and no sect, and something in the mist is eating the reed beds. Nobody with a badge will come, it says, because nobody with a badge has ever heard of Reedwater. Please.

choices.text: Fly to Reedwater

effects.log: You find a poor isle, a frightened child called Moa, and the mist. You stay.

choices.text: Send the crane on to a faction

effects.log: The crane comes back unopened a month later, bedraggled. Nobody else will go.

events.text: Whatever was in the mist at Reedwater is gone, and the reed-folk set a feast for you, all they have. At the same time {ln_order} hears a drifter has done its work on an isle it had forgotten it claimed, and sends an envoy to complain. The envoy is given the seat of honour. You are given the bottom of the table, by the envoy's request.

choices.text: Sit at the bottom, and eat well

effects.log: You eat with Moa and the children at the bottom. It is the best end of the table.

choices.text: Point out whose work it was

effects.log: The reed-folk say it for you, loudly. The envoy leaves early.

events.text: Word spreads along the cloud roads: there is a drifter who comes when the badged will not. Cranes start to find you, from isles you have never heard of. {ln_peer}, another drifter, catches you up on the road and offers to split the work, and the cranes. 'Two rogues,' {ln_peer} says, 'are almost a faction.'

choices.text: Take {ln_peer} on the road

effects.log: You drift together. The isles call you the Two from Nowhere, fondly.

choices.text: Keep the road alone

effects.log: You keep it alone. {ln_peer} goes the other way and you trade letters.

events.text: {ln_order} sends for you, formally: it would be pleased to offer the Known Drifter a badge, a hall and a rank. In return the cranes come to the order first, and the order decides which isles are worth answering. Moa, grown now, writes from Reedwater to ask if you will still come when the crane is from somewhere small.

choices.text: Refuse the badge and keep the cranes

effects.log: You refuse. The order is offended, and the small isles keep sending cranes.

choices.text: Ask for a badge with no strings

effects.log: The order laughs. Badges are strings. You go back to the road.

events.text: A bad year on the Isles: the Sky Rift opens wide, and isles with factions are defended by their factions. Isles without are not. You and every drifter you know hold the poor isles alone for a season. When it is over the factions take the credit at the Jade Court, as factions do, and nobody thinks to mention you.

choices.text: Let them have the credit

effects.log: The poor isles know. You find you only cared what they knew.

choices.text: Speak at the Court for the drifters

ok.log: You speak, and the Court records the drifters by name. A first.

fail.log: The Court notes your remarks and files them under miscellaneous.

events.text: A crane comes from {ln_order} itself: one of its own outposts is lost in the mist, and its elders are trapped there, the same elders who sat you at the bottom of the table at Reedwater. No badged immortal will go; it is too far, too poor, too dangerous. The order asks the drifter, stiffly, by name.

choices.text: Go and bring them out

ok.log: You bring them all out. The elders bow, very low, to a rogue.

fail.log: You bring most of them out, and a wound you carry a century.

choices.text: Send word to the other drifters and go together

effects.log: A dozen rogues bring the elders home. The order cannot thank one without thanking all.

events.text: They call you the Unbound Immortal in the wine houses now, and get the stories wrong. The factions still will not seat you at the top of a table. Moa has a child, who is learning to fold paper cranes. You sit on the Reedwater shore at dusk, a drifter with no badge, and the reeds have never grown so tall.

choices.text: Teach the child to fold a crane that flies

effects.log: The first crane the child folds flies straight to you. You keep it.

choices.text: Write down the true stories, for the drifters after you

effects.log: A book for those with no badge. It is passed from rogue to rogue for ages.

choices.text: Drift on, at dawn

effects.log: You go at dawn, as drifters do. Reedwater keeps a chair for you.
